update description: This sub-process now requires that statistical outputs and dissemination artifacts (reports, tables, dashboards, etc.) are designed using automated and AI-augmented tools—generating templates, metadata, and system specifications in standardized, machine-actionable formats (e.g., APIs, open data, comprehensive metadata). An explicit early review is embedded to determine what product types are needed, with a tendency to exclude unnecessary items, focusing only on those that add value or are required. Outputs are digital-first, discoverable, and optimized for both human and machine consumption. Staff (such as the Data Production and Dissemination Officer) are expected to focus on metadata QA, user-centricity, and tailoring outputs for compliance and client needs.

7 (Disseminate phase) – all dissemination workflows assume standardized, automated-ready outputs
impact reasoning: The Data Production and Dissemination Officer's work shifts from manual editing/creation of outputs to oversight/validation/QC of AI-generated templates/products, with greater emphasis on confirming metadata standards, reviewing product catalogues, and selecting the most user-valuable (or compliant) output types—including early decisions around visualization and digital delivery formats. There is a reduction of hands-on formatting and a new responsibility for filtering output types based on user/parliamentary needs or self-serve capacity, as well as increasing involvement in ensuring machine-actionable and metadata-rich delivery.

gaps.description: Ability to configure or specify AI/digital system generation of custom outputs based on user/client need, including interactive input to templates or automated workflows.

update description: Dissemination components must now be built or reused with automation, modularity, machine-actionability, and seamless API integration at their core. Outputs—from web services and open data to maps and microdata—are generated, versioned, and updated through AI/automation-enabled systems with consistent standards. The officer’s work is now largely focused on technical QA, policy compliance, exception management, and optimizing automation pipelines (rather than manual or ad hoc assembly/release of products).

The role expands to auditing and improving pipelines, specifying and validating exceptions, and overseeing the effectiveness of digital dissemination modules (including troubleshooting or refining for non-standard cases). Less time is spent on direct dissemination work and more on oversight, requirements gathering for modularization, and user feedback for improvements.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities: 'Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data.'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Shifts to ensuring QA, machine-actionability, and compliance of outputs published by automated dissemination modules; less manual formatting or ad hoc release, more focus on confirming process consistency and standards adherence.

affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: In addition to traditional quality review, must assess if dissemination components and their data products are compliant with open standards, machine-readable formats, robust metadata, and can be consumed/triggered using APIs and digital platforms.

gaps.name: Machine-actionable and interoperability standards
gaps.description: Working knowledge of open data standards, APIs, metadata protocols, and automated/digital system QA.

affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Contributes to and delivers training on automated dissemination systems, API-based delivery, use of modular tools, and standards compliance, rather than only manual process guides.

gaps.justification: Materials and training now focus on automation systems, not “manual how-to.”
gaps.name: Training in automation and digital dissemination
gaps.description: Knowledge and ability to explain the operation, limitations, and QA of automation-based dissemination, including use of API endpoints, automated version control, and exception handling.

update description: Statistical outputs—including tables, charts, dashboards, narrative summaries, and methodological documentation—are now generated through AI/LLM-automated pipelines. Human officers are primarily responsible for reviewing, refining, and tailoring these AI-generated drafts, particularly for audience specificity, advanced topics, and clarity. Creating original outputs is minimized, focusing instead on oversight, contextual adaption, and user-centered quality control.
interdependencies: 2.1 (Design outputs and dissemination) – quality of auto-generated outputs depends on templates/metadata developed upfront.
3.3 (Reuse/build dissemination components) – technical outputs are created in the format dictated by automated component designs.
impact reasoning: The officer's job pivots from manually producing statistical tables/reports to reviewing, editing, and adapting draft outputs, narratives, and dashboards generated by automated/AI systems. Specialized tasks now include checking AI-generated methodological descriptions, ensuring outputs reflect the correct analytic process, and refining written/visual content for audience needs and accessibility. They must recognize the limitations of AI-generated results, adapt language/tone/context, and highlight inaccuracies or areas needing human elaboration.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities: 'Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data.'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Focuses on editing/validating draft outputs auto-generated by AI/LLM systems, with less hands-on original creation of content. Increases the need for critical review and QA of analytics and narrative reports.

gaps.justification: Officer must be able to review, correct, and approve machine-generated outputs, which requires understanding both their structure and potential errors/limitations.
gaps.name: Automated output QA and refinement
gaps.description: Skill in systematically reviewing and validating AI/LLM-generated analytics, summaries, dashboards, ensuring clarity, rigor, and fitness for purpose.

affected work-description elements.element: Technical Activities: Communication: 'Drafts reports and articles on the interpretation and use of statistical data and the concepts, methods and techniques used.'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Role changes from manual drafting to reviewing and contextualizing AI-generated reports/articles, ensuring methodological accuracy, narrative clarity, and client relevance.

gaps.justification: Officer must bridge between automated drafts (which may lack nuance/context) and the communication needs of diverse audiences.
gaps.name: AI-generated narrative adaptation
gaps.description: Knowledge of how to review, edit, and translate AI/LLM-produced documentation for clarity, appropriateness, and full methodological transparency.

affected work-description elements.element: Technical Activities: 6. Research and analysis: 'Summarizes and describes meaning of data.'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Instead of original summary, the officer assesses, tailors, and contextualizes AI-generated summaries for accuracy, audience comprehension, and statistical integrity.

gaps.justification: Critical thinking is needed to augment, clarify, and correct draft outputs—recognizing where the machine narrative may be insufficient or misleading.
gaps.name: Critical interpretation and user-centered adaptation of AI output
gaps.description: Ability to assess machine-generated descriptive content for context, accuracy, messaging, and usability, making modifications for diverse stakeholders.

update description: Output validation is now performed using automated, AI/ML-powered digital workflows. Routine comparison, anomaly detection, benchmarking, and quality checks are executed by machine-driven QA tools. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer’s role centers on inspecting and adjudicating complex or ambiguous automated validation results, refining validation protocols, and supporting the continual improvement of the machine validation systems.
interdependencies: 6.1 (Prepare draft outputs) – Ensuring AI-generated outputs conform to the appropriate quality and validation protocols.
3.3 (Reuse/build dissemination components) – Ensures that validation is integrated with dissemination QA workflows.
impact reasoning: The bulk of statistical validation, comparison, and anomaly detection is performed by automated systems. The Officer’s focus shifts to interpreting flagged cases, evaluating the adequacy and effectiveness of automated QA, updating validation thresholds, and feeding insights back into the refinement of validation algorithms/rules. Domain expertise is leveraged in the review and contextual analysis of validation exceptions, validation protocol design, and determining when a human resolution is required.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities: 'Reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases.'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Shifts from hands-on validation/checking to reviewing, adjudicating, and contextualizing automated QA results; involved in refining validation standards, thresholds, and escalation criteria.

gaps.justification: Officer needs skills in interpreting automated QA diagnostics, anomaly/outlier reports, and in setting thresholds for further action/escalation.

gaps.description: Ability to read, interpret, and contextualize reports/flags produced by AI/ML-driven QA tools, and determine required follow-up action.

gaps.justification: Must play a role in system feedback—improving AI/ML QA processes based on recurring errors, edge cases, or shifting data/context.
gaps.name: Validation protocol analysis and system feedback
gaps.description: Skill in critically analyzing automated validation rules and procedures, suggesting improvements, and helping tune AI/ML tools for domain needs.

affected work-description elements.element: Technical Activities: 6. Research and analysis: 'Analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability, and appropriateness.'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Now involves oversight of automated validation, focusing on exception handling and improvement of automated benchmarking/consistency logic.

gaps.justification: Officer must know how to guide machine-driven evaluation and provide feedback loops into system learning.
gaps.name: AI/ML validation technique understanding
gaps.description: Understanding of AI/ML approaches to data quality validation, anomaly detection, and benchmarking, with ability to evaluate accuracy and contextual appropriateness.

update description: Disclosure control (confidentiality checks, suppression, perturbation, output review) is now handled by automated, AI-driven privacy and Statistical Disclosure Control (SCD) tools. All automated actions are logged and auditable. Only outputs with ambiguous, non-standard, or elevated disclosure risks are routed to human experts—whose role is to review, adjudicate, and document final decisions, ensuring compliance and transparency.
interdependencies: 2.1 (Design outputs and dissemination) – proper output standardization is needed to support SCD automation.
6.1/6.2 (Prepare/Validate outputs) – Privacy risks must be included in each output's validation and narrative documentation.
impact reasoning: The Data Production and Dissemination Officer’s activities move away from routine hands-on disclosure control to a more specialized oversight/reviewer function. They intervene only when automated tools flag outputs as ambiguous, non-standard, or at high risk (including new types of data, complex geospatial visualizations, or specialty microdata). Responsibilities now center on investigating and adjudicating privacy flags, approving suppression/perturbation choices, and providing rich documentation and audit trails for controversial or complex cases.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities: 'Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data.'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Editing and validation tasks are now centered on reviewing disclosure and privacy compliance in automated outputs; typical manual intervention is for flagged exceptions.

gaps.justification: Officer must interpret and adjudicate complex AI-flagged disclosure risks, often in new, ambiguous, or critical cases.
gaps.name: Advanced disclosure risk adjudication
gaps.description: Ability to review and resolve uncertainty in privacy/SCD actions taken by AI, including nuanced judgment in ambiguous or novel output types.

The position must have a particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data to ensure their own actions are in compliance.'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Role pivots to ensuring automation aligns with all applicable privacy/SCD legal/policy frameworks, and to documenting, auditing, and justifying human interventions for privacy compliance.

gaps.justification: The Officer must audit, validate, and, if needed, modify the rationale and documentation auto-generated by SCD tools, ensuring compliance.
gaps.name: Automated SCD systems and audit trails
gaps.description: Understanding of how privacy/SCD tools function, what is logged, and how to document, supplement, or override their actions and rationales in complex compliance scenarios.

update description: Finalising outputs is now driven by digital automation; routine collation, checks, and documentation for dissemination are handled by workflow tools. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer reviews flagged anomalies, oversees QA, signs off on release, and handles exceptional or nuanced outputs. The role emphasizes verification, user-centered quality assurance, and expert release decision-making for complex scenarios.
interdependencies: 6.1 (Prepare draft outputs) – Officer’s final QA depends on the quality of prior AI-generated outputs and supporting metadata.
6.2 (Validate outputs), 6.4 (Apply disclosure control) – Officer must ensure validation and privacy results are included in release decisions.
7 (Disseminate phase) – Approved output feeds directly into digital, automated dissemination workflows.
impact reasoning: The role’s manual compilation work is replaced by the need to verify, approve, and (where necessary) adapt final product packages. QA responsibility increases—Officer must ensure outputs are correct, clear, well-documented, and comply with all requirements. Officer addresses, resolves, or escalates exceptional cases (unexpected output, multi-lingual issues, or politically sensitive releases). Collaboration with digital dissemination platforms and internal stakeholders for complex outputs becomes more prominent.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities: 'Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data.'

The officer’s work transitions to oversight and improvement of these real-time digital dissemination platforms, policy and standards guidance, exception/issue management, and advanced user support.

update description: Output systems and databases are updated via automation: data and metadata are loaded, formatted, linked, and validated automatically for API- and AI-driven dissemination. All outputs are automatically checked for metadata enrichment and discoverability. The Officer’s role is to oversee the metadata enrichment and linkage processes, ensure technical correctness, and verify that outputs meet modern machine-actionable and discoverability standards prior to release.

7.2 (Produce dissemination products) – Outputs can only be published if metadata/linking checks are complete and compliant.
impact reasoning: Manual loading, formatting, and cross-linking of data and metadata is displaced by technical QA and oversight activities. The Officer is increasingly responsible for verifying that automations, schemas, and standards are correctly applied by the system—ensuring that all outputs are ready for API, AI, and human consumption. They must be able to audit compliance, troubleshoot digital linkage issues, and advise both users and IT specialists on discoverability or format-related exceptions.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities: 'Prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata.'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Role pivots to meta-validation: checking completeness, enrichment, API/AI actionability, and automated linkage of metadata; less hands-on, more oversight/troubleshooting/reporting.

gaps.justification: Need to understand, audit, and validate compliance with digital/automated metadata, linkage, and discoverability standards.

gaps.name: API/automation output consulting and troubleshooting
gaps.description: Skill in supporting, diagnosing, and optimizing access to outputs for both human and automated users in a digital, API-first landscape.

Human officers serve as reviewers, validators, and final adapters—ensuring all products meet publication standards and audience requirements before digital release. 7.1 (Update output systems), 7.3/7.4 (Release/Promote products) – Only validated products flow forward for digital release and communication.
impact reasoning: Manual creation and formatting of dissemination products are replaced with review and adaptation of AI-generated outputs—including narrative, visualizations, and microdata products. The Officer’s contribution shifts to focused quality control, standards validation, publishing compliance, and adapting or customizing outputs for specific user or release needs. Additionally, maintaining familiarity with the automated product pipeline and troubleshooting or enhancing system performance is essential.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities: 'Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data.'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Primary tasks now involve reviewing for adherence to publication, meta, and audience-specific standards; less generation by hand, more focus on standards QA, final adaptation, and sign-off.

gaps.justification: Must be able to interpret, critique, and adapt a wide range of AI/automation-derived outputs (text, graphics, microdata, etc.) for diverse audiences.
gaps.name: AI/automation output review and adaptation
gaps.description: Skill in systematically reviewing, validating, and customizing AI/LLM-generated dissemination products for publication, metadata, and audience standards.

update description: All elements of dissemination product release—including scheduling, embargo management, access provisioning, and confidential data controls—are automated. Digital orchestration platforms manage, log, and execute real-time releases. Data Production and Dissemination Officers primarily manage exceptions: overseeing complex or high-profile releases, handling retractions or errors, and liaising with privileged user groups for special access needs.
interdependencies: 7.1 (Update output systems), 7.2 (Produce dissemination products) – Only fully validated and packaged products are eligible for automated release.
6.5 (Finalise outputs) – Exceptional or sensitive releases require additional review/approval.
impact reasoning: Manual intervention in standard releases is no longer required; the role pivots to oversight of automated releases, quality and policy approval for embargo or sensitive products, and direct support for high-profile users (press, government, researchers). Collaboration with platform managers, policy staff, and senior subject-matter experts is more common, especially for error recovery (retracts) and non-standard circumstances.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities: 'Participates on data production and dissemination teams.'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Role focuses on policy review, exception workflows, and special-case product releases (e.g., embargo, retraction, or high-visibility clients), much less on routine operational work.

gaps.justification: Officer needs skills in navigating, auditing, and managing digital release workflows and exception approval, as well as in communicating with high-level clients.
gaps.name: Exception management and high-visibility release liaison
gaps.description: Ability to review and approve exception cases in digital orchestration systems, and to coordinate confidential/embargoed or impactful public releases with stakeholders.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities: 'Provides statistical data and consultative services to users.'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Duties now center on high-level user support and consultation (e.g., secure research access, press briefings for embargoed releases, subscriber communications), as standard release channels are largely hands-free.

gaps.justification: Greater responsibility for managing access for diverse, privileged user groups in API-enabled, secure digital environments.
gaps.name: Secure access management and client liaison
gaps.description: Skill in granting, auditing, and managing secure digital access to confidential or embargoed data, and in advanced client communication for sensitive releases.

The Officer’s role is to review, validate, and optimize high-profile, complex, or sensitive communications—focusing on effectiveness, compliance, and reputation protection for the organization.
interdependencies: 7 (Disseminate phase overall) – Promotion approaches must be harmonized with automated release, cataloguing, and platform logic.
Communication and training duties – Officer’s review of promotional content often extends to audience support and expectation management.
impact reasoning: Routine campaign creation, channel selection, and message deployment are replaced with QA, optimization, and exception oversight for AI-generated content. The Officer must understand how to evaluate AI recommendations, provide feedback or edits for context/accuracy/compliance, and step in for sensitive campaigns or when automation produces questionable or reputationally risky material. There’s greater emphasis on analytic review of outreach effectiveness and learning from AI system outputs.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities: 'Markets and disseminates data.'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Role shifts to reviewing and optimizing AI-generated outreach campaigns across platforms, and taking ownership for sensitive or high-impact communications.

gaps.justification: Must critically evaluate and intervene on AI-prompted messages for clarity, alignment, and risk.
gaps.name: AI-generated communication QA and optimization
gaps.description: Skill in reviewing, validating, and adapting content, strategy, and channel selection generated by AI for promotional outreach, including campaign performance monitoring.

affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Work shifts to editing/validating AI-generated language for promos and assuring correct interpretation/messaging in outreach products.

gaps.justification: Reviewing, customizing, or rejecting AI-generated marketing and communication text requires greater skill in risk assessment, narrative tone, and public/audience centricity.
gaps.name: AI-generated messaging evaluation
gaps.description: Knowledge of effective AI-driven outreach strategies, and how to review, adapt, or supplement messaging for interpretation accuracy, compliance, or complex audience needs.

update description: User support for dissemination is now routed through AI-powered chatbots and digital interfaces, which answer routine questions, triage support requests, and guide users in real time to statistical products, metadata, or publications. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer is escalated only complex, nuanced, or high-value queries. They additionally curate the knowledgebase (FAQ), review and improve chatbot output, and analyze feedback to strengthen AI-assisted support over time.
interdependencies: 7 (Disseminate phase), 6.1/6.5 (Prepare/finalize outputs) – Effective support is cross-dependent on current product metadata, documentation, and release practices.
Quality management – User input via support escalates to process improvement for product and service delivery.
impact reasoning: Routine helpdesk and FAQ queries are taken over by chatbots and automation, freeing the Officer for complex troubleshooting, client advocacy, and improving digital support tools. Activities increasingly involve curating detailed and updated FAQ/knowledgebase entries, overseeing AI/cognitive chatbot accuracy, and working closely with IT and service design on escalations, user training, and forward-facing outreach.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities: 'Provides statistical data and consultative services to users.'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Most queries are routine and answered by automation. Officer’s consultative role is reserved for escalated, non-routine, nuanced, or strategic requests, as well as designing/curating advanced support pathways.

gaps.justification: Officer requires skill at diagnosing and resolving complex digital support issues, including those only surfaced after automation fails.
gaps.name: Complex support case management
gaps.description: Ability to handle, resolve, and document nuanced, ambiguous, or policy-sensitive user issues, working in tandem with automated systems and tracking knowledgebase/FAQ impacts.

affected work-description elements.element: Technical Activities: Communication: 'Provides input to training material and assists in the delivery.'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Provides ongoing review of AI-generated knowledge articles, populates advanced FAQ material, and supports training/advice for both users and staff in the new automated support ecosystem.

gaps.justification: Greater need for digital literacy in chatbot/AI knowledge curation, and in content review/editing for automated support channels.
gaps.name: AI chatbot/knowledgebase management
gaps.description: Proficiency in reviewing and editing AI-generated FAQ content, training staff and power users on automated support, and feeding user insights back into digital service design.
